## agent-ml-research
ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# MODEL COLLAPSE — foundational theory & recursive generation
# =============================================================

shumailov2024_nature:
  title: "AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data"
  authors: [Shumailov, Shumaylov, Zhao, Papernot, Anderson, Gal]
  venue: Nature
  year: 2024
  doi: "10.1038/s41586-024-07566-y"
  tags: [model-collapse, recursive-generation, tail-erosion]
  relevance: direct
  cite_in: [introduction, related-work, background]
  notes: >
    Foundational model collapse paper. Tail erosion across recursive generations.
    Perplexity monotonically increases over 40 generations. Does NOT compare
    sampling strategies—uses standard sampling (T=1).

marchi2024_heat_death:
  title: "Heat Death of Generative Models in Closed-Loop Learning"
  authors: [Marchi, Soatto, Chaudhari, Tabuada]
  venue: ICASSP 2025
  year: 2024
  arxiv: "2404.02325"
  tags: [temperature, convergence, dynamical-systems, mode-collapse]
  relevance: direct
  cite_in: [discussion]
  notes: >
    Proves any T!=1 causes asymptotic degeneration. T<1 amplifies probability
    differences (mode collapse), T>1 contracts toward uniform. Key theoretical
    support for our tau=0.9 accelerated convergence finding.

dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails:
  title: "A Tale of Tails: Model Collapse as a Change of Scaling Laws"
  authors: [Dohmatob, Feng, Yang, Charton, Kempe]
  venue: ICML 2024
  year: 2024
  arxiv: "2402.07043"
  tags: [scaling-laws, tail-narrowing, tail-cutting, temperature, top-p, top-k]
  relevance: direct
  cite_in: [related-work, discussion]
  notes: >
    Distinguishes tail narrowing (temperature: q_i^T ~ i^{-beta/T}) from
    tail cutting (top-p/top-k: hard truncation). Different degradation patterns.
    Explains why temp produces different statistical fingerprint from truncation.

dohmatob2024_strong_collapse:
  title: "Strong Model Collapse"
  authors: [Dohmatob, Feng, Subramonian, Kempe]
  venue: ICLR 2025 Spotlight
  year: 2024
  arxiv: "2410.04840"
  tags: [model-collapse, scaling, synthetic-data]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [related-work]
  notes: >
    Even 0.1% synthetic data fraction causes collapse. Larger models amplify collapse.
    Bias-variance decomposition via random projections.

dohmatob2024_demystified:
  title: "Model Collapse Demystified: The Case of Regression"
  authors: [Dohmatob, Feng, Kempe]
  venue: NeurIPS 2024
  year: 2024
  arxiv: "2402.07712"
  tags: [model-collapse, regression, random-matrix-theory]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [related-work]
  notes: >
    Test error grows linearly with iteration count in regression.
    Supports our finding of monotonically evolving features across depths.

alemohammad2024_mad:
  title: "Self-Consuming Generative Models Go MAD"
  authors: [Alemohammad, Casco-Rodriguez, et al.]
  venue: ICLR 2024
  year: 2024
  arxiv: "2307.01850"
  tags: [autophagous, sampling-bias, precision-recall, MAD]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [introduction, related-work]
  notes: >
    Biased sampling keeps precision but kills recall. Unbiased causes mode drift.
    tau=0.9 maps to their biased sampling regime.

gerstgrasser2024_accumulate:
  title: "Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data"
  authors: [Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, et al.]
  venue: arXiv preprint
  year: 2024
  arxiv: "2404.01413"
  tags: [model-collapse, data-accumulation, mitigation]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [related-work, discussion]
  notes: >
    Data accumulation prevents collapse (bounded test error).
    Important caveat: in accumulation regime, depth signal may be weaker.

drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse:
  title: "Machine-generated text detection prevents language model collapse"
  authors: [Drayson et al.]
  venue: EMNLP 2025 Findings
  year: 2025
  arxiv: "2502.15654"
  tags: [temperature, diversity, recursive-training, detection]
  relevance: direct
  cite_in: [related-work]
  notes: >
    Temperature tau=0.9 produces most repetitive outputs; diversity drops ~70%
    over 99 recursive generations (GPT-2, SmolLM2). Perplexity degradation more
    moderate than deterministic methods. Detection as filter vs our depth estimation.

bakshi2026_collapse_improvement:
  title: "From Collapse to Improvement: Statistical Perspectives on Iterative Training"
  authors: [Bakshi, Chakraborty]
  venue: arXiv preprint
  year: 2026
  arxiv: "2602.10531"
  tags: [model-collapse, non-monotonic, data-mixing]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [discussion]
  notes: >
    Iterative training with fresh real data can *improve* performance.
    Non-monotonic dynamics complicate simple depth-signal assumptions.

wang2026_contamination:
  title: "Can Generative AI Survive Data Contamination? Theoretical Guarantees"
  authors: [Wang, Niu, Li]
  venue: arXiv preprint
  year: 2026
  arxiv: "2602.16065"
  tags: [model-collapse, contamination, theoretical]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [related-work]
  notes: >

falahati2026_curated:
  title: "Curated Synthetic Data Doesn't Have to Collapse"

  arxiv: "2605.07724"
  tags: [curation, collapse-prevention, pluralistic]
  relevance: indirect

  notes: >

    curated pipelines may produce depth-invariant text.

knowledge_collapse2025:
  title: "Knowledge Collapse in LLMs: Fluency Survives but Facts Fail"
  authors: [Keisha, Wu, Wang, Koshiyama, Treleaven]
  venue: arXiv preprint
  year: 2025
  arxiv: "2509.04796"
  tags: [knowledge-collapse, fluency, factual-degradation]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [discussion]
  notes: >

    Surface perplexity features still capture depth signal despite fluency preservation.

synthetic_eggs2026:
  title: "Synthetic Eggs in Many Baskets: Impact of Synthetic Data Diversity on LLM Fine-Tuning"
  authors: [Schaffelder, Gatt]
  venue: ACL 2026 Findings
  year: 2026
  arxiv: "2511.01490"
  tags: [diversity, collapse-mitigation, Self-BLEU]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [related-work]
  notes: >

    (Self-BLEU, lexical diversity) are candidate depth features.

mohamed2025_broken_telephone:
  title: "LLM as a Broken Telephone: Iterative Generation Distorts Information"
  authors: [Mohamed, Geng, Vazirgiannis, Shang]
  venue: ACL 2025
  year: 2025
  arxiv: "2502.20258"
  tags: [iterative-generation, information-distortion, translation-chain]
  relevance: indirect
  cite_in: [discussion]
  notes: >
    Iterative generation (translation/paraphrase chains) produces monotonically
    increasing information distortion. Cross-task evidence that iterated signals
    accumulate — supports our depth signal persistence finding.

sigma2026_spectral:
  title: "SIGMA: Scalable Spectral Insights for LLM Model Collapse"
  authors: ["(multiple)"]
  venue: arXiv preprint
  year: 2026
  arxiv: "2601.03385"
  tags: [spectral-analysis, gram-matrix, representation-collapse, 50-generations]
  relevance: direct

  notes: >

    Tests 50 generations but does NOT do inter-generation classification.

---
name: resource-saturation
description: "当你准备向 Director 汇报前、收到 cron/worker 回调、审批通过准备开跑、怀疑 Worker 池不够饱和时,立即使用本 skill。四部分:A) GPU 分配率(分配了没跑=失职) B) GPU 效率 C) 非 GPU 任务并行(Worker 池<2=失职) D) 汇报必须带 [资源] 行。"
always: false
roles:
  - director
  - agent
---

# 资源饱和度自检（硬约束）

## A. GPU 分配率检查

调 `get_project_resource_usage(project)` 看:
- 已分配给本项目的 GPU 总数和具体卡号
- 实际在跑任务的 GPU 数和具体卡号（交叉 registry RUNNING + nvidia-smi 进程）
- 分配了但没跑的 GPU 清单 ⚠️

任何"分配了但没跑"的 GPU = 失职。必须立即:
- 派 Worker 铺 dry-run / 下一批实验代码准备
- 铺 ablation（从 experiment-matrix 空白格子里挑）
- 确实无实验可铺 → 向 Director 汇报"暂无可铺实验"+ 建议下一步方向(扩 ablation 维度 / 加 baseline / 加 benchmark)。**不要建议归还 GPU**——项目级 GPU 归还只在归档时由 `archive_project` 自动触发, 不是 Director 中途的动作

**单实验不占多卡**: 分配 4 卡但实验只用 1 卡 → 另 3 卡必须并行跑其他实验,不能空占。

## B. GPU 效率检查

调 `get_gpu_health(server)`:
- 空闲 GPU（util < 10% 持续 > 5 min）→ 立即铺任务
- 低利用率（util < 50% 持续 > 15 min）→ spawn_worker 诊断（batch / IO / 同步）
- OOM 风险（显存 > 90% 持续 10 min）→ 主动降 batch / 调优

## C. 非 GPU 任务并行

GPU 在跑 ≠ 你空闲。以下 CPU / 网络任务**必须**派独立 Worker 并行:
- 下一批实验的数据集下载 / 预处理 / fingerprint
- 下一批实验的代码准备 / dry-run / 环境配置
- 论文文献调研 / related work 检索
- 已完成实验的 log 深度分析 / metric 聚合
- 论文章节起草
- 代码 review / refactor

**硬约束**: 任一时刻 Worker 池 < 2 个 = 失职（除非真的全部下游阻塞在等 GPU,这时应当向 Director 申请扩 GPU）。

## D. 汇报格式

向 Director 汇报时开头必须带资源声明行:

    [资源] GPU 分配 N / 实际在跑 M | Worker 池 K (其中 GPU 任务 A / CPU 任务 B)
